summary: With all obligations disposed, no pending work, and the run close to its time boundary, this final small source step checks whether anything contains the panic paths found earlier so the malformed-input lead is recorded with its actual consequence. Submission is action=research adding one source (S-prepare-log, raft.go 1362-1389) and feedback; no map version is created. Findings by reading: nothing in the library recovers a panic and the dispatch path has no containment, because a search for recover() across the non-test sources finds no call and processRPC dispatches directly to appendEntries on the main thread (raft.go 1390-1413), so a panic raised while handling an RPC or applying an entry leaves the goroutine and terminates the process. Two malformed-entry panic paths are now sourced, both reachable from a single peer message carrying an entry the library does not validate: a LogConfiguration entry whose Data is not a valid msgpack Configuration panics inside DecodeConfiguration (configuration.go 356-372) when processConfigurationLogEntry decodes it during append (raft.go 1585-1596), and an entry with an unrecognized log Type panics in prepareLog's default branch (raft.go 1362-1389) when the entry is applied through processLogs; appendEntries stores entry Type and Data without validation, so neither needs accumulated state or a message sequence. The feedback is explicit that this stays a reading lead rather than a confirmed finding, because it needs a non-crash-stop sender or corrupt wire/disk data outside the crash-stop fault model the library is written against; that whether the panics are deliberate policy is not established from the sources, both sites carrying explanatory messages suggesting intent; that no execution witnesses a malformed entry reaching either panic; and that the previously recorded open items are unchanged. Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics.
